items.headline: QUT report maps six governance priorities for councils rolling out AI
items.summary: Researchers at QUT's City 4.0 Lab / Urban AI Hub have published 'Responsible Artificial Intelligence in Local Government', a report examining how councils across five countries (including Australia) are already using AI in customer service, planning enquiries, infrastructure and environmental management. It argues AI adoption is outpacing the governance needed to use it responsibly, and sets out six priorities: clear accountability, organisational capability, data and technical safeguards, transparency and human review, community participation, and workforce preparation. The work was widely republished across the sector on 10-11 August via The Conversation, Route Fifty and Mirage News.
items.so_what: This gives any Australian council standing up AI in statutory or customer-facing work a ready-made governance checklist to pressure-test its own approach, rather than building one from scratch. It also points to transferable local examples worth studying: Brimbank City Council's computer-vision cameras on waste-collection vehicles that flag damaged roadside assets (an asset-management dividend from an existing fleet), and the City of Stirling's AI-supported resident-engagement platform for consultations. It is a framework and awareness signal, not a proven product, so its value is in shaping policy and procurement before a council scales AI.
